title: Reading Between the Lines of Academic Articles
text:
Academic articles are written to report original research, and they follow a predictable structure. Most begin with an abstract that summarizes the study, followed by an introduction that establishes the research gap. The methodology section explains how the data were collected, which allows other scholars to evaluate the reliability of the findings. Readers who understand this structure can locate key information far more efficiently.

However, the conclusions of an article are not always as definitive as they appear. Authors often use hedging language, such as 'may suggest' or 'appears to indicate', to signal that their claims are tentative. Recognising these cautious expressions is therefore essential, since overlooking them can lead a reader to overstate what the study has actually demonstrated.

questions.text: According to the passage, what does the abstract of an academic article do?
options: It explains how the data were collected

questions.text: According to the passage, why do authors use hedging language?
options: To prove that their findings are definitive
To signal that their claims are tentative

questions.text: What can be inferred about a reader who ignores hedging language?
options: They will always reach the correct conclusion
They may overestimate what a study has shown
They will read the methodology more carefully

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the methodology section, as implied by the passage?
options: To summarize the study in a few sentences
To state the authors' personal opinions
To let other scholars assess the reliability of the findings

vocabulary.definition: a system of methods and procedures used in research
the quality of being trustworthy and consistent
not yet certain or fixed; open to revision
to present something as more important or certain than it really is

paragraph_translations: Los artículos académicos se escriben para informar sobre investigaciones originales y siguen una estructura predecible. La mayoría comienza con un resumen que sintetiza el estudio, seguido de una introducción que establece el vacío de investigación. La sección de metodología explica cómo se recopilaron los datos, lo que permite a otros académicos evaluar la fiabilidad de los hallazgos. Los lectores que comprenden esta estructura pueden localizar la información clave con mucha más eficiencia.

Sin embargo, las conclusiones de un artículo no siempre son tan definitivas como parecen. Los autores suelen usar un lenguaje de cautela, como 'may suggest' o 'appears to indicate', para señalar que sus afirmaciones son provisionales. Reconocer estas expresiones cautelosas es, por tanto, esencial, ya que pasarlas por alto puede llevar al lector a exagerar lo que el estudio realmente ha demostrado.
